meta.title: Introduction to Spreads
meta.description: Learn what a spread is — Vivid's core data primitive. Three SpreadNoise operators generate variable-length float arrays that drive Metaball circles on screen.

sticky_notes.text:
**What is a Spread?**
A spread is a variable-length array of floats —
Vivid's core data primitive. Even a single
value is a spread of length 1. This graph
uses three 8-element spreads to animate
8 circles on screen.

**SpreadNoise → X positions**
Generates 8 animated noise values
used as X coordinates. Each element
drifts independently, creating organic
horizontal motion.

**SpreadNoise → Y positions**
Same operator, different seed so
Y motion is independent of X.
Together they create 2D wandering.

**SpreadNoise → Radii**
Smaller amplitude (0.06) keeps radii
visible but subtle. The circles gently
breathe as values animate.

**3 spreads flow into Metaball**
pos_x, pos_y, and radii each receive
8 values. Metaball draws one circle
per element — element 0 gets
(x[0], y[0], r[0]), and so on.

**Circles + Rainbow mode**
Each ball gets a unique hue from the
Rainbow color mode. Try switching
render_mode to Metaball to see the
classic blobby look!
